content: The immunoglobulin A (IgA) antibody, which plays a critical role in mucosal immunity, was identified by David Rowe and John Fahey. Immunoglobulin D (IgD) was also identified by the same researchers. Immunoglobulin E (IgE), a class of antibodies primarily involved in allergic reactions, was discovered by K. Ishizaka and T. Ishizaka. Further genetic studies elucidated the underlying mechanism responsible for the immense diversity of antibody proteins. This diversity was found to arise from somatic recombination of immunoglobulin genes, a groundbreaking discovery made by Susumu Tonegawa in 1976.
